title: Stage 2: TCO calculator
description: On-road price, energy cost from state prices and real-world mileage, maintenance curve, insurance, probability-weighted battery replacement, financing interest, minus present-value resale. Outputs total TCO, ₹/km, break-even month vs petrol baseline.
notes:
Implemented in src/lib/engine/tco.ts against fixtures. The bd dependency on u90 was a data dependency, not a code one — the engine is pure by design and takes the reference tables as plain data, so the calculator is written and mutation-tested without them. Validation against real curves belongs to u90 + the golden fixtures task (znc).

Modelling choices worth knowing before they are hard to change:
- Financing is modelled as cash out, not as a loan schedule: TCO carries on-road price + interest paid within the horizon + processing fee. Down payment, EMIs and the principal outstanding at exit net to exactly that, so a tenure running past the horizon needs no special case.
- Only the resale credit is discounted (tables.discountRatePct). It is the one large flow landing entirely at the far end; running costs are quoted nominally because that is what a buyer plans against.
- Insurance renewals are the state's first-year rate applied to the depreciated value. We hold no premium curve, and this is the only renewal model the tables support.
- Battery replacement tapers to zero over the last 2 years of the hold (TCO_CONVENTIONS.batteryReplacementTaperYears) because owners at that point sell rather than replace. Warranty coverage (years AND km) zeroes it outright.
- Price escalation is 0 and stated as an assumption. No sourced curve exists, and a flat rate moves every candidate the same way — totals change, order does not.
- Electricity slab selection stays in the query layer: it needs a household base load the profile does not carry.

title: E20 assessment rules engine + tests
description: Deterministic verdict from compatibility data + emission norm rules (BS-VI phase 2 compliant; BS-VI 2020-23 E10-tuned; BS-IV and older material concerns). Emits verdict, mileage-delta range, risk level, inspection checklist, service-interval adjustment.
notes:
Implemented in src/lib/engine/e20.ts with 63 tests. The dependency on 8un was a DATA dependency, not a code one — the engine is pure by design and takes e20_compatibility and e20_guidance_rules rows as plain data, so it is written and tested against fixtures without the dataset. Curating 8un supplies rows; it changes no code here.

Resolution order, and nothing lower can override something above it: powertrain (diesel/EV/hydrogen settle it outright, flex-fuel is compliant by construction), then the compatibility table, then the emission-norm rule, then unknown. FR-B5 is a real answer, never a fallback guess.

Decisions worth knowing before they are hard to change:
- CNG and LPG are assessed as bi-fuel, not not_applicable. Every factory fitment sold in India keeps a petrol tank, so the blend reaches the engine; an assumption is emitted saying so, and naming the gas-only conversion case the assessment does not cover.
- FR-B3 is tested as window INTERSECTION with the manufacture year, not containment. We hold a year and rows hold dates, so a row running from April 2023 does describe some 2023 vehicles. Partial overlap is used and declared; discarding it would answer unknown for vehicles we do have data for.
- Material risk escalates one level past 15 years but NEVER from a none base. A vehicle certified E20-material-compliant has no ethanol-specific exposure to compound, and inventing one would contradict its OEM position (FR-B9).
- Mileage delta falls back to the verdict's typical band when a row carries only one bound, because FR-B6 requires both. The substitution is declared as an assumption.
- The norm rule yields medium confidence for BS-VI phase 2 (a type-approval requirement applied to the whole class) and low for every other norm, which infer from the ABSENCE of a requirement.
close_reason: Engine implemented and tested; remaining dependency 8un is data curation, not code.

title: blendedEfficiency arithmetic-means kmpl, overstating economy on every candidate
description:
src/lib/engine/tco.ts:201 computes the city/highway blend as `city * share + hw * (1 - share)` — a weighted ARITHMETIC mean of km-per-unit. Fuel consumed over a mixed route is `d_city/e_city + d_hwy/e_hwy`, so the distance-weighted blend the doc comment describes is the HARMONIC mean: `1 / (share/city + (1-share)/hw)`.

Arithmetic mean >= harmonic mean always, so the current form systematically OVERSTATES efficiency, and therefore understates energy cost, cost/km, break-even month and gCO2e/km. The error grows with the city/highway spread, so it does not cancel across candidates — it biases the ranking toward variants with a wide spread.

Feeds both computeTco (tco.ts:413) and computeCo2 (co2.ts:372), so it moves the cost AND environment sub-scores together.

Worked example: 12 kmpl city / 18 highway at 20% city over 252,000 km. Arithmetic gives 16.8 kmpl and 15,000 L; the true figure is 16.36 kmpl and 15,400 L — 400 L, about 2.7%, roughly Rs 42,000 of fuel understated over the horizon. A 14/20 SUV at 60% city is understated by 3.1%.
acceptance_criteria: blendedEfficiency returns the harmonic distance-weighted blend; single-figure fallback and the null case are unchanged; tco.test.ts and the golden snapshots are re-derived from the corrected arithmetic.
close_reason: Closed

title: sameColumnValue does not defend against Postgres scale-rounding
description: src/db/seed/provenance.ts:133. sameColumnValue defends against Postgres zero-padding but not scale-rounding, so an authored value with more decimal places than the column's scale compares unequal to what Postgres stored. The diff then rewrites the row on every seed run and churns provenance rows that did not actually change. Found by adversarial review of CarbonMiles-e9r.
acceptance_criteria: An authored value that Postgres rounds to the column scale compares equal to the stored value and produces no diff.

title: Paise safe-integer guard misses money columns not named *Paise
description: src/db/seed/provenance.ts:274. The guard selects columns with field.endsWith('Paise'), so any money column named otherwise skips the safe-integer check entirely. Money is bigint paise precisely because a rupee figure past int32 drifts once compounded over a ten-year horizon; a money column that evades the guard reintroduces exactly that. Found by adversarial review of CarbonMiles-e9r.
acceptance_criteria: Every money column is guarded regardless of its name — driven off the schema's column type rather than a name suffix.

title: fact_provenance row goes stale when a fact value changes but its evidence block does not
description: src/db/seed/provenance.ts:394. A fact whose value changes while its evidence block is unchanged leaves the old fact_provenance row current, so the row cites evidence for a value that is no longer there. This defeats the point of per-field provenance: the number a user sees would carry an attribution to a source that documented a different number. Found by adversarial review of CarbonMiles-e9r.
acceptance_criteria: Changing a fact value supersedes its prior fact_provenance row even when the evidence block is byte-identical.

title: Marketing site: full-viewport deck landing page
description:
A presentation-style marketing site at /. Each fold fills the viewport and advances one at a time, ending on a 'Try now' call to action.

Decided with the user 2026-08-23:
- Advance on SCROLL AND KEYBOARD ONLY. No click-to-advance and no right-click-to-advance: right-click would mean suppressing the browser context menu sitewide, which breaks copy / open-in-new-tab / inspect and reads as a broken page.
- 'Try now' links to /login and nothing more is built. That route does not exist yet and will 404 until Epic 6 (CarbonMiles-837, email OTP) lands. This is deliberate, not an oversight.

Content must come from 'Carbon Miles.md' and docs/PRD.md — the two journeys are the Vehicle Purchase Advisor and the E20 Compatibility Advisor. No invented statistics, testimonials or partner logos on a real product's landing page.
design: Next.js 16 App Router. Scroll-snap or an equivalent that degrades to ordinary scrolling when JS is unavailable or prefers-reduced-motion is set, rather than a hijacked wheel handler that traps the user. Folds are real sections with real headings so the page stays navigable by keyboard and screen reader.
acceptance_criteria: Each fold fills the viewport and advances on wheel/trackpad and on arrow, space, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End. prefers-reduced-motion falls back to normal scrolling. Every fold is reachable by keyboard alone. The final fold's 'Try now' navigates to /login. Verified in a real browser, not just by build success.
close_reason: Deck landing page built, verified in Chrome via Puppeteer (22/22 checks: wheel + trackpad-cadence advance, all keyboard keys, 8/8 folds keyboard-reachable, Try now to /login, reduced-motion fallback, short-viewport safety valve) and committed as 110c81d. Two unsupported copy claims filed separately as CarbonMiles-4ui and CarbonMiles-0li.

title: db:validate --write-quality: recompute data_quality rows
description:
`pnpm db:validate` (scripts/validate-data.ts, task 53m) is deliberately read-only: it reports and exits, it never writes.

DATA-MODEL.md describes `data_quality` as "recomputed by the validation job", and its columns (score, missingFields, staleFields, computedAt) map almost exactly onto what the report already computes per table. But CLAUDE.md treats database writes as deliberate transactional acts, and a reporting command with a silent side effect is worse than a missing feature — so the write was left out rather than smuggled in.

Follow-up: add an explicit `--write-quality` flag that, in one transaction, upserts a data_quality row per entity: score = completeness x source tier x recency, missingFields from the per-column completeness pass, staleFields from the staleness pass. Until then data_quality stays empty and nothing reads it.

Note the engine reportedly uses data_quality to break ties between otherwise equal vehicles, so this blocks that tie-break being real.

title: Backfill llm_calls.costMicroUsd from gateway getGenerationInfo
description: src/lib/ai/telemetry.ts captures providerMetadata.gateway.generationId on every call but ships costMicroUsd: 0. The AI SDK returns no cost in-band; the only real source is gateway.getGenerationInfo({ id }) -> totalCost (USD), which needs an AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY or OIDC (a Vercel access token is not enough). Add an out-of-band job that resolves cost per generationId and updates the row via usdToMicroUsd(). Do NOT hardcode per-token prices - that is fabricated data and rots silently. Blocked on generationId being persisted somewhere (it is currently carried on LlmCallRecord but has no llm_calls column).

title: Project serviceCentreCount and resale liquidityScore into the scoring input
description:
Stage 3 (src/lib/engine/stage3.ts) takes ScoringInput.serviceCentreCount and ScoringInput.resaleLiquidityScore as plain nullable numbers, because the engine never imports src/db/. Nothing supplies them yet.

serviceCentreCount lives on manufacturers, two joins away from vehicle_variants (variant -> model -> manufacturer). liquidityScore lives on resale_curves and is deliberately NOT on the engine's ResaleCurvePoint type, so the query layer has to read it from the same row that priced the residual — otherwise the liquidity score and the residual can come from different segment/fuel/asOf rows and silently disagree.

Until this lands, both dimensions score null for every candidate and their weight is redistributed. That is correct behaviour, not a bug, but it means reliability and resale currently contribute nothing to any ranking.
design: Project in src/lib/data/, not in the engine. Reuse the resale curve row already selected by computeTco rather than re-querying, so the two figures cannot drift apart.
acceptance_criteria: A recommendation run populates both fields for candidates whose manufacturer and resale curve rows carry them, and the resulting sub-scores are non-null. The liquidity score comes from the same resale_curves row as the residual.

title: Seed emission_factors rows with sources and provenance
description: co2.ts takes emission factors as data by design; the rows do not exist yet. Needs petrol/diesel/CNG per-unit factors and a state-varying grid factor, each with a sourceId and a fact_provenance row, plus the EthanolBlend inputs (ethanol fossil well-to-tank and biogenic tailpipe figures, and the E20 efficiency penalty from e20_compatibility.mileageDelta*Pct). Until these are seeded, computeCo2 correctly refuses rather than guessing.

title: Licence-class (GVW) filter for commercial profiles
description: Stage 1 filters commercial candidates on payloadKg only. GVW is the other hard constraint a fleet buyer lives with: an LMV licence tops out at 7500 kg GVW in India, so a variant above that is unbuyable for an owner-driver who holds one. CandidateVariant deliberately omits gvwKg today because commercialProfileSchema has no licence-class field to filter it against — adding the column without the profile input would be a dead field. Needs: a licenceClass enum on the commercial profile branch, gvwKg on CandidateVariant, and a hard filter with its own exclusion code.
acceptance_criteria: A commercial profile declaring an LMV licence excludes variants over 7500 kg GVW, with a reported reason; an unstated licence class filters nothing.
